translit:
sarav dise ekakar | upadhi mite nahi andhala ||
sutra bhidi sab ek | pan juda juda ambala ||129||
nir vana jaise nadi | aiso hari vana bhekh ||
bij khoyo mulgo | boho suko khet ||130||
murakh mantra chudiya | samajhethi thay bhut ||
moh liyo mele nahi | jyun maru ko unt ||131||
mugat kahe sab bhekh | lei duniyano asro ||
murakh na jane maram | lidho pasaro suthro ||132||
bhekh keso vavek | jo sanakadik sanse padya ||
isht tano adhikar | apanpe sarav atalya ||133||
mala pahere be char | manman harakhe murkha ||
e gatradani nar | phokat deva pharadka ||134||
veshya tano vyabhichar | bahu sabad shravane suno ||
taryo na ek lagar | jam kam rat vina kamni ||135||
jog vagoyo kanye | indri eke nav thari ||
eh lagyo apradh | atam vagoyo andhale ||136||
baiyar kahai mati mahro | ma kahe maro put ||
mati su mati mali | atam rahyo abadhut ||137||
nari to nirdokh | vishnu bhagat jo upaje ||
nahi to vyai bhund | jangal jangal bhatakat phare ||138||
guru tano pratap | khaye roto rabdi ||
pet tano parpanch | ghere gher kidhi mavdi ||139||
ene so apradh | murakh nar kan parhare ||
nadi tanan je nir | jai gangaman bhale ||140||
purav pakh dekhie | ja mukh ved vistar ||
so ghat bhitar pekhie | atam tano adhar ||141||
bhagvant bhane nahi bhat | pet tana parpanch ||
murakh seve manavi | chhandi kamlakanth ||142||
bhate padi vat | devi daladrane olgi ||
sua datar kartar | khole gali gosli ||143||
gadhvi ghelo kanye | harijansu hansi kare ||
marag bhulyo mudh | jam kankar puthe phare ||144||
brahmanpe bharda bhala | je bhagar magi khay ||
brahman na dije bethne | prit de lagay ||145||
kunkumka tika kiya | bhardako so ang ||
kulkarni chhute nahi | jyun bhagtan bhele bhand ||146||
tirath sab sanse padyan | jan ave mat koy manhe ||
karma hamne lagsi | jo pade viprki chhanhe ||147||
anant kot vasidado | sakal pakhka mul ||
narsingh ghat ghat pekhiye | gaya te sanse sul ||148||
sapt dvip navkhandlu | vyapak jaka rup ||
shankh chakra su dekhiye | narsingh anopam rup ||149||
narsingh nirbhe sitapati | manman soch bichar ||
bharme bhulyo atma | pan sadguru sabde par ||150||
narsingh nirbhe koy nahi | jake bhram guncha bhel ||
sab kari dese ekatun | jaise ghritman tel ||151||
prahlad kaj pravesh | khambhman khunkhariyo ||
na ayo bhagtansu bhid | shun budho thayo ke hari gayo ||152||
sabki jivan ramji | ram santanke das ||
e barad tabko liyo | jab narsingh bhaye prakash ||153||
shankhasur karan shurmo | peth gayo patal ||
nir udadyo puchh kar | tab dariye mani har ||154||
dhruv avichal raj | ekvisme brahmand tape ||
sant tano mahimay | e kahiye mahatam te khape ||155||
kalo muhdo kan e | hanuman taro kyam thayo ||
e lagyo apradh | je natarang jova rahyo ||156||
ram kahat shi laj | mukhthi na bole murkha ||
jare jam grahese kesh | kem bubadi padesh bapda ||157||
shaligram seve sada | man kherka khut ||
atho por lado paro | jyun maruko unt ||158||
sakhi sabdi het kar | mil kar gaiye git ||
rab roto mil paiye | e parmeshwarni prit ||159||
panthi chalyo panthsir | joi godad khat ||
pau palakke panch dinman | uth chalege bat ||160||
ghano na ghales bhar | brahman vaniya dubla ||
am tan kaise jor | sahej sanjage je mala ||163||
vaniyo kare vyapar | agho pachho osre ||
kripanath kripal | jane male nav male ||162||
je ape adar kari | god pasari leu ||
vast thorki thor hai | trikha hoy so piu ||163||
bhikhari bhagvantka | tuka de so khau ||
man apman kachhu nahi | harkhe hari gun gau ||164||
mala tilak tano mahimay | tribhuvanman sancharyo ||
janak jam tano vivad | tare e pragat karyo ||165||
mala pahere ek | bahu mala te shun kare ||
bhramar jive sab vas | phul khay te aphare ||166||
tadh nashe tapne | tem hari name apradh ||
rat divas na meliye | sant samagam sadh ||167||
gadh lidho kahe gumar | chhatrapati ko na vaso ||
sarav sarikhdo sath | ek bhastan sahu bhaso ||168||
baher tyagi dekhiye | manhe mayani bhukh ||
do do batan kyun bane | jam golman chuk ||169||
maya brahma nahi jujvan | jyun paniman dudh ||
murakh pive ek kari | koy sant valove sudh ||170||
padmani pichhe padi | kubja agel kod ||
tuti luli pangli | pan pakdi hariki ot ||171||
mansa devi upni | tathe bhayo omkar ||
ghat ghat hari vyapi rahyo | so khele nand dvar ||172||
brahma ved vistar te | shukdev shrimukh boliyo ||
nirakar nij rup | so dvare dvare doliyo ||173||
damodar dayal | je ap bandhave damne ||
jamla arjan karne | bandhyo bandh ja chhodve ||174||
bijo kalo barne | kale kalo je tare ||
kalo kamlakanth | kale kele ko tare ||175||
baiyan biji var | nahi ave aiso davdo ||
maya malse kani var | pan nahi hoy sant melavdo ||176||
kahane kidhu kaher | al sarikho aniyo ||
sahuko jane pindar | pan tribhuvannath na janiyo ||177||
baio kero betdo | dhoyo pana bai ||
kali kutumbman jivna | vaishnavjini sagai ||178||
thorun bolethi rahese | vade so avichal ven ||
dridh kachha kar varsna | sakhi tohe tharanda nen ||179||
uttam jansu prit kar | jyun prem badhanto thay ||
nich sangat akhar sabad | so ghatat ghatat ghat jay ||180||

|| iti shri vaishnav jivandasji na doha sampurna ||
translation:
129. Everything is seen as one single form; but for the blind man the veil of adjuncts (upadhi) never lifts. Strung on one thread they are all one, yet each amla bead stays separate.

130. As a river is without water, so is religious garb without Hari. He lost the original seed and sowed a dry field.

131. The fool has been snared by charms and mantras; by his own [mis]understanding he turns into a ghost. Whatever infatuation has seized, he will not let go, like a Marwari's camel.

132. Every wearer of religious garb claims liberation, while leaning on the world for support. The fool does not know the secret; he has merely spread out a tidy display.

133. What discrimination is there in outward garb, when even Sanaka and the other sages fell into doubt? Claiming the authority of their chosen deity, they have measured everything by their own selves.

134. He wears two or four rosaries and the fool rejoices inwardly. He is [like] a woman of Gatrada [unclear], making empty flourishes for nothing.

135. It is the harlotry of a prostitute: he hears many words with his ears and is not carried across even a little, like a woman without desire in the act of love.

136. Why did you squander yoga? Not one of the senses came to rest. This offence has clung to you: the blind man has ruined his own soul.

137. The wife says "he is my husband (mati)," the mother says "he is my son." Clay (mati) merged back into clay; the soul remained an avadhut, untouched.

138. A woman is blameless if a devotee of Vishnu is born of her; otherwise she has littered like a sow, and [her offspring] wander roaming from jungle to jungle.

139. In the name of the guru's glory he eats his bread and gruel; it is the fraud of the belly - he has made a "mother" of house after house.

140. For this offence, why should the foolish man be cast off? The waters of a river, once they enter the Ganga, become good.

141. Look to the earlier tradition, from whose mouth the Vedas spread out. Behold Him within this body-vessel - He is the support of the soul.

142. The bard does not sing of God; it is all the fraud of the belly. The fool serves human beings and abandons Kamalakanth (Lakshmi's lord, Vishnu).

143. The bard has laid out his road: he has waited upon the goddess of poverty. The true giver is the Creator, yet he goes about the open lanes and alleys [unclear].

144. Why is the Gadhvi (bard) so crazed that he mocks the devotees of Hari? The dolt has lost the road; Yama's servants follow at his heels.

145. Better than a brahmin is the bharda who begs his fasting-grain and eats it. Do not seat the brahmin beside you and give him your affection.

146. Marks of kumkum have been made all over the bharda's body. His hereditary calling will not leave him, like a buffoon mixed in among devotees.

147. All the places of pilgrimage have fallen into doubt; let no one go inside them. Karma will cling to us if we fall under such a brahmin's shadow.

148. Endless crores [of appearances] are so much sweepings; the root of every sect is one. Behold Narsingh (Narasimha) in every heart, and the thorn of doubt is gone.

149. The seven continents and the nine regions - His form pervades them all. He is seen with conch and discus: Narsingh, of matchless form.

150. Narsingh is the fearless one, the lord of Sita; reflect and consider this in your mind. The soul has strayed in delusion, but by the Satguru's word it crosses over.

151. None is fearless like Narsingh; for the one whose delusion is a tangled knot, He will make all things one, as oil merges into ghee.

152. For Prahlad's sake He entered the pillar and roared out of it. No hardship ever fell upon His devotees - has He now grown old, or has He been defeated?

153. Ramji is the life of all; Ram is the servant of His saints. He took this vow from the time when He shone forth as Narsingh.

154. For the sake of Shankhasur the hero went down into the netherworld. He flung the waters up with his tail; then the ocean admitted defeat.

155. Dhruv's kingdom is unshakable; he shines in the twenty-first sphere of the universe. Such is the greatness of a saint - it is worth telling, and telling it serves its purpose.

156. Hanuman, why did your face turn black? This fault clung to you - that you stayed on to watch the dance-show.

157. What shame is there in saying "Ram"? The fool will not utter it with his mouth. When Yama seizes him by the hair, how will you howl then, poor wretch?

158. He worships the shaligram stone always, but his mind is a stump of hard khair wood. All eight watches of the day he goes about loaded down, like a Marwari's camel.

159. With love [sing] sakhis (couplets) and shabads; let us meet and sing the song together. Let us share gruel and bread together - this is the love of the Lord.

160. The traveller has set out on his road, having seen [only] a quilt and a cot. In the blink of an eye, within five days, he will rise and walk his way.

163. [printed number; the sequence indicates 161] Do not load on too heavy a burden - brahmins and banias are frail. What strength has a body like ours? Whatever comes together comes of itself, naturally.

162. The bania drives his bargain, going forward and drawing back again. The gracious Lord of mercy - who knows whether He will be found that way or not.

163. Whatever is given with respect, I take with my lap spread open. The thing stays in its own place; let the one who is thirsty drink.

164. I am God's beggar; whatever crumbs are given, that I eat. Honour and insult are nothing to me; joyfully I sing Hari's praises.

165. The glory of the rosary and the tilak has spread through the three worlds. In the dispute between Janak and Yama, this was made manifest.

166. Wear one rosary - what will many rosaries accomplish? The bee lives entirely on fragrance; the one who eats the flower is left bloated.

167. As cold is driven off by a fire, so are sins driven off by Hari's name. Night and day do not let go of satsang (holy company) and the company of sadhus.

168. In his conceit he says "I have taken the fort," though the sovereign's rule is not his at all. The whole company is of one kind: when one barks, all bark.

169. Outwardly he looks a renunciate, but inside is a hunger for maya. How can these two go together? The slip lands one in Yama's snare.

170. Maya and Brahman are not two separate things, like milk in water. The fool drinks them mixed together as one; some rare saint churns out the pure.

171. The padmini, the perfect beauty, was left behind; Kubja's longing went ahead. Broken, crippled and lame she was, yet she caught hold of Hari's shelter.

172. From the mind (mansa) the goddess arose, and from her came Omkar. Hari pervades every heart, and He is the one who plays at Nand's door.

173. The expanse of Brahman and of the Vedas - Shukdev spoke it from his own blessed mouth. The formless One, in His own nature, wandered from door to door.

174. Damodar the compassionate, who let Himself be bound with a cord - for the sake of the twin Yamalarjun trees He was bound, only to loosen their bondage.

175. Another dark one stands at the door; by the Dark One the dark is carried across. Dark is Kamalakanth; by a mere dark plantain who can cross over? [unclear]

176. Sisters, such an occasion will not come a second time. Maya will be met with many times over, but a gathering of saints will not come again.

177. Kanha (Krishna) worked havoc; He was keen as a needle's point. Everyone took Him for a herdsman, but no one knew Him as the Lord of the three worlds.

178. He is the women's little boy; [unclear]. In the household of the Kali age, Jivan says, kinship is with the Vaishnavs.

179. If one speaks little, what is spoken will stand as unshakable words. Make your resolve firm and let it rain down [unclear]; then, friend, your eyes will find rest.

180. Make friendship with the highest people, so that love goes on increasing. In low company the letter and the word keep dwindling, until they dwindle away to nothing.

|| Here end the dohas of Shri Vaishnav Jivandasji, complete. ||
